Title: Proposed Scope Tagging
Description: Lets Open Box record, on either side of the taxonomy, where discovery analysis has identified potential value add beyond what the client does today. Modelled as a flag orthogonal to the existing coverage and scope tags, so the current-state tag is preserved and the today-versus-proposed delta stays visible.
Acceptance Criteria: A process can be flagged Proposed Scope in both the Value Streams and MRI PMX System views; the existing coverage/scope tag is retained; proposals are visually distinct from agreed scope.

Title: Flag a value-stream process as Proposed Scope
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want to flag a value-stream process as Proposed Scope, so that I can record where Open Box believes MRI PMX could add value beyond the client current way of working.
Acceptance Criteria: A Propose control appears on each card in Edit Mode; flagging it does not change the coverage tag; the card shows both tags together (for example "Outside" alongside "PROPOSED"); the flag is saved with the version.

Title: Flag an MRI PMX system process as Proposed Scope
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want to flag a system process as Proposed Scope, so that I can recommend PMX capability that is not in the agreed implementation scope.
Acceptance Criteria: A Propose control appears on each system card in Edit Mode; the existing scope tag (Core / Custom / Out of scope) is retained; the proposal is saved with the version.

Title: Capture the value-add rationale for a proposal
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want to record why a proposal adds value, so that the recommendation carries a business case rather than just a label.
Acceptance Criteria: Both edit modals expose a Proposed Scope checkbox and a rationale field; the rationale appears in the detail panel and in the generated document; a prompt appears when a proposal has no rationale; unticking clears the rationale.

Title: Distinguish a proposal from agreed client scope at a glance
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want Open Box proposals to look clearly different from agreed scope, so that a client can never mistake a recommendation for something they have signed up to.
Acceptance Criteria: Proposals use a distinct marker and dashed treatment, differing by shape as well as colour so they stay legible for colour-blind readers; the detail panel states the current state and that the item is a recommendation, not agreed scope.

Title: Bulk-propose or clear proposals for a column
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want to propose or clear a whole column at once, so that I can tag quickly during a discovery workshop.
Acceptance Criteria: The Tag all menu in both views offers Propose all and Clear proposals; both apply to every process and sub-process in the column; existing coverage and scope tags are left untouched; the action costs one undo step.

Title: Filter both views by Proposed Scope
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want to filter to just the proposals, so that I can review the full value-add story with a client.
Acceptance Criteria: A Proposed Scope toggle appears in both view filter bars; it narrows the existing coverage/scope selection rather than replacing it; it shows the whole proposal footprint including link-implied items; scope-count chips report direct and implied counts separately.

Title: Clear proposals when loading the Discovery Baseline
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want the Discovery Baseline to start with no proposals, so that each new client engagement begins from a clean sheet.
Acceptance Criteria: Loading the Discovery Baseline clears item proposals and proposed links on both sides; the agreed link set is left intact; reset behaviour respects the active baseline.

Title: Proposed Scope Propagation Across Links
Description: Carries a proposal across the existing business-to-system links so it only has to be captured once, deriving the other side rather than storing it. Derivation is deliberately limited to one hop: propagation is bidirectional, so a stored flag would cascade through the link graph (system items average 5.9 business links, maximum 16) and a single click could have proposed a third of the taxonomy.
Acceptance Criteria: Flagging either side marks its linked counterparts as implied; implied items never imply further items; implied markers self-correct when links change.

Title: Imply a proposal across links in both directions
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want a proposal on one side to mark its linked counterparts on the other, so that I do not have to tag the same recommendation twice.
Acceptance Criteria: Flagging a value-stream card marks the MRI PMX processes it links to as implied; flagging a system process marks the value-stream cards it serves; implied items render hollow and distinct from direct proposals; the tooltip and detail panel name the origin and its rationale.

Title: Prevent proposal propagation from cascading
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want implication to stop after one hop, so that flagging one card does not light up a third of the taxonomy and make the proposals list meaningless.
Acceptance Criteria: Derivation reads only the directly-set flag, never an implied one; a directly-proposed card linked to a high-fan-out system process implies that process and no further items; verified against the busiest link node, where none of the sibling cards sharing it are marked.

Title: Propose a link that does not exist today
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want to mark a link itself as proposed, so that a taxonomy gap becomes a concrete recommendation rather than a blank.
Acceptance Criteria: The Mapping view edit mode offers a proposed toggle on each link chip; proposed links render dashed and distinct from agreed links; the mapping cell legend counts them separately.

Title: Keep proposed links out of agreed-scope derivation
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want a proposed link to have no effect on agreed scope, so that adding a recommendation cannot quietly change the client scope picture.
Acceptance Criteria: Proposed links are excluded from the linked-system-id set and from the has-link check; adding one does not lift an item out of auto out-of-scope; the unlinked warning still appears, and reads "proposed link only" when a proposed link is the only one present.

Title: Value-Add Proposals Document
Description: Turns the captured proposals into a client-facing deliverable, while guaranteeing that an Open Box recommendation can never appear in an agreed-scope document by accident.
Acceptance Criteria: Proposals are excluded from generated documents unless explicitly included; when included, a dedicated section lists each proposal with its rationale, current state and linked counterparts, under an explicit disclaimer.

Title: Exclude proposals from generated documents by default
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want proposals left out of documents unless I opt in, so that a recommendation never appears in a signed scope document by mistake.
Acceptance Criteria: The export options include a Proposed Scope checkbox that defaults to unticked, unlike every other include; with it unticked no proposal content appears in the preview, the Word file or the PDF; the same dataset can therefore produce both an agreed-scope document and a proposals document.

Title: Generate a Value-Add Proposals section
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want a dedicated proposals section, so that I can present the value-add story to a client as its own deliverable.
Acceptance Criteria: With Proposed Scope ticked, the document gains a Value-Add Proposals section grouped by side and module; each entry gives the location, the current state, what Open Box proposes and the rationale; the section opens with a statement that these are recommendations and not agreed scope; the preview and the Word file read identically.

Title: Nest linked counterparts under each proposal
Description: As an Implementation Consultant, I want each proposal to list what it touches on the other side, so that one recommendation reads as one item rather than being counted once per link.
Acceptance Criteria: Each proposal lists its linked counterparts as supporting detail; link-implied items do not get their own entries; proposed links are marked as such in the list.

Title: Security & Compliance
Description: Keeps the application defensible against the security expectations of client due diligence and of Open Box own ISO/IEC 27001 programme. The app is a static client-side tool with no backend, accounts or personal data, so the meaningful controls are secure development, dependency hygiene and documentation rather than infrastructure hardening.
Acceptance Criteria: A current internal assessment exists; no known dependency vulnerabilities; dynamic content is escaped; security policy, licence and secure-development guidance are published in the repository.

Title: ISO 27001 Secure Development Baseline
Description: The assessment and remediation work bringing the repository in line with the applicable ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A technological controls, principally A.8.8, A.8.25 to A.8.32.
Acceptance Criteria: Annex A gap analysis recorded; identified findings either remediated or consciously accepted; npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities.

Title: Produce an internal ISO 27001 Annex A assessment
Description: As Open Box, I want an evidence-based internal assessment of the repository against ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, so that we can answer client due-diligence questions and prepare for certification without overstating our position.
Acceptance Criteria: Assessment covers the applicable Annex A controls with evidence drawn from the repository; states plainly that 27001 certifies an organisation ISMS and not an application, and that the document is a self-assessment rather than a certificate; findings are prioritised with severities.

Title: Resolve known dependency vulnerabilities
Description: As a Developer, I want the dependency tree free of known advisories, so that the supply chain does not become the weakest point of an otherwise low-risk application.
Acceptance Criteria: npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities; fixes prefer the minimum patched version over speculative major upgrades; any transitive pin is documented.

Title: Escape all dynamic content written to innerHTML
Description: As a Developer, I want every interpolation of editable content escaped, so that authored taxonomy content cannot inject markup into the application.
Acceptance Criteria: Every component writing dynamic content to innerHTML routes it through the shared escape helper; editable free-text fields, including proposal rationales, are covered; verified by rendering a script or image payload and confirming it appears as inert text.

Title: Publish security policy, licence and secure-development guidance
Description: As Open Box, I want the repository to carry its own security documentation, so that contributors and reviewers can see the threat model and the reporting route.
Acceptance Criteria: Repository contains a licence, a security policy with a vulnerability-reporting contact, and a secure-development document recording the threat model and secure-coding conventions.
